questions.question: Which invariant makes a CDN checksum a meaningful security control?
options: The delivered bytes match a digest obtained through an independently trusted path
The CDN returns any digest beside the asset
The asset has a short cache lifetime
The file name contains the word secure
questions.explanation: An attacker must not be able to replace both the asset and the expected digest; otherwise a malicious pair can still match.

questions.question: An edge serves altered JavaScript, but authenticated HTML contains the original SRI value. What should the browser do?
options: Execute the script and report later
Block the script because the computed digest mismatches
Replace the HTML digest with the edge value
Ignore the mismatch when TLS is enabled
questions.explanation: TLS protects transport to the selected endpoint, while SRI enforces the expected bytes. A mismatch must block execution.

questions.question: Why is a digest sidecar stored under the same CDN credential as the asset a weak trust anchor?
options: Sidecars cannot contain Base64
The attacker can replace both the bytes and their claimed digest
CDNs cannot cache two files
The digest becomes too long
questions.explanation: Separate objects do not create independent trust when one compromised authority can rewrite both.

questions.question: A SHA-384 digest contains how many raw bytes?
questions.explanation: SHA-384 outputs 384 bits. Dividing by 8 bits per byte gives 48 raw bytes before Base64 encoding.

questions.question: Which release order avoids HTML referencing an asset that has not reached the CDN yet?
options: Publish HTML, then build the asset
Overwrite the old asset URL, then purge later
Upload the immutable asset, verify propagation, then publish referencing HTML
Publish the digest only after users report failures
questions.explanation: The versioned asset and integrity metadata must exist before the document makes that release reachable.

questions.question: A mismatch appears at one CDN point of presence immediately after deployment. What is the safest first response?
options: Disable verification because the event may be benign
Block the asset, scope reports by release and edge, then compare build, origin, and edge bytes
Retry the same mutable URL until it executes
Delete all evidence and rebuild
questions.explanation: A stale or corrupt edge can look like an attack. Enforcement should fail closed while operators preserve and compare evidence.
